match.reason: No single bank point teaches the whole claim, evidence, analysis and link paragraph structure; the closest, topic sentences and supporting evidence, each cover only one part of it, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Building an analytical paragraph
card: It opens the paragraph with one clear claim that answers the question. It tells the reader what the paragraph will prove.
A short example from the text that supports the claim. It can be a brief quotation or a described moment.
It explains how the evidence supports the claim. It names the writer's choice and says what effect it has on a reader.
The last sentence ties the paragraph back to the question, so the reader sees why the point matters.
draft.remember: Claim, proof, explanation, then a return to the question.

a.q: Which part of an analytical paragraph explains how the evidence supports the claim?
a.why: Analysis is where the student says how the writer's choice creates an effect and why that backs the claim. The evidence only supplies the example, so it cannot explain itself.
a.clue: Which part answers the question 'how does this show it?'

b.q: Sam writes a paragraph on how a novel presents loyalty. It has a claim, a short quotation and a sentence on its effect. It ends by describing the next scene. What is missing?
opts: A link back to the question
b.why: The paragraph has a claim, evidence and analysis, but it ends by retelling the plot instead of returning to the question about loyalty. A link is needed to show why the point answers the question. Retelling the next scene adds no link.
b.clue: Check how the paragraph ends, not how it begins.

b.best: A link back to the question
